guard: each of the six spawnable scripts under scripts/ runs its main() both by its real path and through a symlink: both runs reach that script's own refusal (its exit code and a stderr line only main() prints) and agree on exit code, stdout and stderr, rather than exiting 0 having done nothing. The two scripts with no side-effect-free invocation are held to the shared helper only by a one-line source census of top-level scripts/*.mjs; see COVERAGE BOUNDARY
why: THE DIRECTION IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH PROVING. A broken entry guard does not throw, does not
print, and does not exit non-zero: it exits 0 having scanned nothing, which every caller reads
as a pass. Two of the eight scripts are CI gates, so the failure mode is a gate reporting clean
on a range it never opened.
The first three mutations put back the exact guard each file carried, one file at a time,
rather than one mutation over a shared line. The three spellings failed differently and a
reader who only ever saw the template-literal form would conclude the URL escaping was the
whole defect: `pathToFileURL` and `resolve` encode correctly and still compare an alias against
a canonical path, so they break on a symlink alone.
Mutation four is the one that matters most and it is deliberately not a guard: it hollows the
realpath comparison inside `isMainEntry` while leaving the `entry === self` fast path intact.
That is what a plausible simplification of this helper looks like, and it is invisible to any
cell that only ever invokes a script by its real path, since the fast path answers those
correctly. It reddens the symlink half of every parity cell; it names one so the verdict points
at a line rather than at a cascade.
Mutation five grades the CENSUS rather than the scripts. The census is the only cell covering
`post-publish-install-probe.mjs` and `preflight-npm-publish.mjs`, which start their work at
entry with no argv that refuses first, so no probe for them exists that does not pack a tarball
or read the registry. A census reports `clean` on a healthy tree, which is exactly what a census
that has stopped looking also reports, so the planted control is the cell that has to be proven
live. Blinding the reader leaves the census itself GREEN and reddens the control, which is the
shape being asserted.
AGREEMENT IS NOT EXECUTION. As first merged, each parity cell compared the two runs and nothing
else, and two runs that both skip main() agree perfectly: exit 0, nothing on either stream.
Measured against that suite, with a killed control in the same file and the same run: switching
the guard of check-attribution.mjs off by both paths, and making `isMainEntry` answer false for
every invocation, each left it green at 8 of 8. Each parity cell now also requires both runs to
reach that script's own refusal: its exit code and one whole stderr line that only its main()
prints. The exit code alone would not do. With the helper switched off,
`check-attribution.mjs --selftest` exits 0 with no output, the same status a passing self-test
returns, and `live-job-conclusion.mjs` refuses with 1, the status Node also exits with when the
script cannot load at all.
Mutations six to eleven switch the guard of each probed script off by both paths, one file
each, and each names its own cell. That is what grades each cell's witness on its own: a
mutation in the shared helper reddens all six parity cells but grades only the one it names, so
a cell whose expected refusal a skipped main() also satisfies would pass there unseen.
Mutation twelve is the one the review asked for: `isMainEntry` answers false for every
invocation, so no script runs main() by either path. It edits the same file as mutation four
and runs in the same proof, and mutation four is its killed control: that kill shows this suite
reaches `scripts/main-entry.mjs` at runtime, so a survivor here would be a coverage gap rather
than a mutant that changed nothing.
Mutations thirteen to fifteen put back the old guards of the three probed scripts the first
three do not reach. `doc-binding.mjs` asks through a `RUN_AS_CLI` assignment, so its anchor is
that line, and its old spelling brings back the `pathToFileURL` import it needed (an ESM import
declaration is valid anywhere at module top level). `pr-head-gate.mjs` and
`verify-publish-closure.mjs` compared through `resolve`, which both still import.
Mutations sixteen and seventeen grade the two halves of the witness apart, since every mutation
above breaks both at once. Sixteen points the helper import of `live-job-conclusion.mjs` at a
file that does not exist: the script cannot load, exits 1 by both paths with the same stack, and
so matches its refusal's exit code and agrees across paths. Only the stderr line catches it, and
it is the same failure `--preserve-symlinks-main` produces (see COVERAGE BOUNDARY). Seventeen
keeps `check-attribution.mjs` running main() but drops its return value, so both paths print the
usage line and exit 0. Only the exit code catches it.
NOT ASSERTED, and recorded rather than implied: `upgrade-section-gate.mjs` keeps its own inline
copy of the same realpath comparison and is exempted from the census by name. It already has a
cell and a registered mutant of its own (`scripts/mutations/upgrade-section-gate.json`, `a
symlink invocation is mistaken for an import and silently skips the CLI`), and re-pointing
somebody else's proof at this helper would buy nothing here.
COVERAGE BOUNDARY. None of the following is graded here.
- Anything the census cannot see. It reads only top-level `scripts/*.mjs`, one line at a time,
and drops a line by its opening comment token. A guard that reads `process.argv[1]` on one line
and compares it on the next, a file in a subdirectory, another extension, and every guard
outside `scripts/` are invisible to it. The planted controls prove it still refuses the
one-line shape; they do not widen that scope.
- `post-publish-install-probe.mjs` and `preflight-npm-publish.mjs` are held by that census
alone. No cell runs them, through a symlink or otherwise, and no mutation here edits their
guards.
- `isMainEntry` compares realpath strings, not device and inode. Case-insensitive filesystem
aliases and Windows junctions are not exercised.
- Under `node --preserve-symlinks-main` with the link in another directory, the
`./main-entry.mjs` import resolves beside the link. check-attribution, check-operator-literals,
live-job-conclusion and verify-publish-closure then exit 1 with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, where
before the helper each printed its refusal. doc-binding and pr-head-gate fail the same way on
their package imports with or without the helper. The failure is loud, and no cell runs under
that flag.
- The same hand-rolled comparison is still live outside `scripts/`, for example in
`packages/seat/src/custodian.ts` and `examples/05-scale-showcase/src/{swarm,observe}.ts`.
Nothing in this suite reads those files.
NO `completionMarker` and no `progressPattern`. The suite runs every cell and prints one line
each, so a mutation that reddens several is still readable as reddening the one it names, and
the summary line is printed on a red run too.
